A 29-year-old G1P1 woman at 36 weeks of gestation attends a routine prenatal visit with no specific
complaints. Her medical history includes mild asthma controlled with a rescue albuterol inhaler and a
large submucosal uterine leiomyoma surgically removed via open myomectomy two years ago. She
has received regular prenatal care but missed some appointments during the second trimester. Her
temperature is 97.4°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 150/82 mmHg, pulse is 64/min, and respirations are

16/min. She experiences mild shortness of breath while speaking, but no crackles or wheezing are
noted on lung examination. A grade 2/6 systolic flow murmur is present on cardiac examination. The
uterine fundal height measures 36 cm, and fetal heart rate is 150 beats/min by Doppler. The patient
reports occasional contractions over the past week without fluid leakage. What is the most appropriate
next step in managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Perform a biophysical profile to assess fetal
well-being (B) Administer Rh(D) immunoglobulin (C) Induce labor with oxytocin infusion (D) Perform an
amniocentesis to assess fetal lung maturity (E) Deliver via cesarean section (C-section) (F) Administer
corticosteroids to promote fetal lung development (G) Continue with routine prenatal care while
awaiting spontaneous labor (H) Schedule an elective cesarean section at 39 weeks gestation (I)
Perform a trial of labor despite prior uterine surgery (J) Initiate magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection
 A. Continue with routine prenatal care while awaiting spontaneous labor
B. Perform a trial of labor despite prior uterine surgery
C. Administer corticosteroids to promote fetal lung development
D. Initiate magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection
E. Perform an amniocentesis to assess fetal lung maturity
F. Perform a biophysical profile to assess fetal well-being
